questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I’m in koreanstudies therefore going to on exchange is mandatory, but obviously its something we all look forward to, especially to enhance our language skills.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The school helped us so so so much, and it really made the exchange so much better. It will probably always be a bit overwhelming to live in a new country and culture, but jeju university really helped us making it as easy as possible for us, and helped foster friendships with the local people in our classes.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Well i arrived in Korea at the end of covid so informations were very clear at that point, it also helped that we were in contact with the university. But i feel exchange is a stressful process due to all the applications and so on that needs to be done both to the home university and exchange university.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: The school had a contact person from the office we could text at all times if we had problems to help us navigate everything, and they also gave us a ‘buddy’ who was one of their students who we could also contact to help us out, and then they granted each buddy money for us to go experience the place were i was exchange. They also helped us make our residence card and bank are at the school, they really couldn’t have been more helpful.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: There were only dormitories

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: Many different meal plans for the school cafeteria

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: It’s very convenient, i had a great experience with it but i also had a good roommate. Be aware of the rules the curfew rule you can bend, but mixing boys and girls are a big no go (people got kicked out for that). I arrived 2 weeks before school start and the rooms still hadn’t been cleaned from the people living there before me, so even if they ask and pressure you to move in early (which cost extra, we didn’t know) then you don’t have to.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Im not sure what you mean by this question. But the registration was out application we sent moths in advance. They wanted quite a lot of medical stuff which was a bit hard to get doctors here at home to do but otherwise everything was good.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: A contact person??

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: This was amazing actually, we got a list of classes we could take and then we got first access to them. So all the exchange students got the classes they wanted. (Don’t know if this is different now though)

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I guess just know your information, and it helps if you are more people to go, if you keep contact and help each other out, everything will work out.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: They were English so the level of language was medium because I’m already fluent in English which was a good advantage, but the courses were topics i never would be able to study here so i really enjoyed that, i also had korean language and my teacher there was just so amazing, i learned so much.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: I really enjoyed it because it was easy to take notes to, and the exam would essentialy be everything the teacher said in class so i just had to keep studying that.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Korean language, jeju seen from a world perspective, The Korean Wave and Culture Trends, Analyzing K-Movie Culture

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: All of them, they were interesting and unique to that university

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Not unexpected necessarily, but its commonly known food is very cheap in Korea but when you have to buy every meal out it gets really expensive still

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Grocery shopping is more expensive compared to eating out. And small things like toothpaste and deodorant is way more expensive there than in Denmark.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: They made 4 field trips and one sports day while we were there, there was also a 3 day school feastival, and later a street food festival and world food festival. So many many activities for us. There was also a teacher (he’s not there anymore) who facilitated many extra activities, we had a culture day were we cooked food repressed by 3 countries, and much more.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The field trips, and the school festival.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go out and experience all the nature jeju has, it’s incredible. We climbed Halla mountain (which is the biggest in South Korea) and went to many beaches and caves and so on.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Personally i had quite a hard time in the beginning, i was on an island as maybe 1 out of 5 people with blonde hair and blue eyes so it was very intimidating being so perceived at all times. But after i settled it was fine.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: It helps doing activities the school offers you, that’s where i met almost all my friends.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: there's small things like they don't have grocery shops but small convenience stores which i had to get used to as well.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The food!!!!!!!! And people’s friendliness and kindness when trying to speak their language.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: It might be stressful at times, but everything will always work out, you will always find a solution, so take a deep breath and enjoy the trip of your life, you will meet people and experience things you will hold on to for a long time. Find a community, that may be your friends from Denmark or the other exchange students in your class, or local students, but this is sooo important because these are the people you create memories with and it’s so helpful to have each other when you have remember or do practical things, both school like deadlines or exams but also applications relating to the exchange (Also emotional support)

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Ask the year before what their experience or application process was like. It might be different for you but it’s nice to get an idea of what to expect when you know nothing.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: All the friendships i got from all over the world. And the language skills

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Finding emotional support when your established support system is so far away, that’s also why i say it’s important to create your own little community while you’re there.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
